title: A Yearbook for the Tryouts
premise: Odile Voss runs an anonymous account that exposes the rot beneath her small town's beloved tradition: the annual 'Tryouts,' a yearbook-adjacent competition that decides who gets scholarships, internships, and a future. When her civics teacher pairs her with Theo Marsh—the golden boy whose family built the Tryouts—for a semester project on civic institutions, Odile must investigate the very machine she's been tearing down, alongside the person it was built to crown. As they uncover that the Tryouts have been rigged for generations to protect a handful of families, their uneasy alliance deepens into something neither of them can afford. In the end, Odile chooses to unmask herself publicly rather than let Theo take the fall, and together they rebuild the Tryouts as something honest—winning justice outside the law and each other against all duty.
about_author: J. M. Voss is a former debate coach who grew up in a town where one competition decided everyone's future. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to accept the rules they were handed.

chapters.title: Anonymous, Obviously
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She posts another takedown of the Tryouts from her anonymous account @yearbookghost, then navigates school as her invisible self while her best friend Priya begs her to be careful. Beat: establish her double life and the thrill of hidden power.

chapters.title: Assigned Seating
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Mr. Okafor announces semester projects in pairs; Odile draws Theo Marsh, heir to the Tryouts dynasty. Their first meeting is pure venom—he assumes she's slacking, she lets him. Beat: collision of worlds, mutual contempt.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He drags Odile into the yearbook archive for research and catches her lingering over a 1987 Tryouts photo where someone's name has been inked out. Beat: first crack of curiosity between enemies.

chapters.title: @yearbookghost
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo discovers the anonymous account and becomes obsessed with its accuracy, quoting it in class without knowing he's complimenting his partner. Odile nearly chokes. Beat: dramatic irony tightens.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The pair interviews the Tryouts committee and notices the scoring rubric is sealed. Priya warns Odile she's getting too close to exposure. Beat: stakes sharpen; friendship strain.

chapters.title: Inked Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They identify the blacked-out name: Dana Reyes, a winner erased after questioning the judges. Dana now works at the diner and refuses to talk. Beat: the past reaches forward; reluctant alliance forms.

chapters.title: Study Session, Unsupervised
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Late-night library session; Theo admits his father scripts his entire future around winning the Tryouts. Odile almost tells him about the account. Beat: vulnerability, first real connection.

chapters.title: The Rubric Leak
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile's source inside the administration sends her the sealed rubric—and evidence scores were altered last year. She must decide whether to publish or protect the investigation. Beat: moral fork in the road.

chapters.title: Homecoming Interference
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At homecoming, Theo's father publicly humiliates Odile as 'charity case' material. Theo defends her, shocking everyone including himself. Beat: love against duty ignites; public lines drawn.

chapters.title: Dana Talks
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Dana finally reveals she was erased because she found proof of rigged judging in 1987—and that the same families still control the committee. Beat: the conspiracy gains shape and history.

chapters.title: Ghost Hunted
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The committee hires someone to trace @yearbookghost. Theo realizes with horror how much the account knows about things only Odile could know. Beat: suspicion turns inward; dread builds.

chapters.title: The Almost-Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. On the roof after a project win, Odile and Theo nearly kiss, then nearly confess everything else. Both retreat. Beat: romantic peak undercut by fear; tension doubles.

chapters.title: Priya's Ultimatum
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Priya finds Odile's burner and gives an ultimatum: tell Theo the truth or end it. Meanwhile the committee announces this year's Tryouts will 'modernize'—with new surveillance of students. Beat: pressure from every side.

chapters.title: Traced
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The investigator delivers a name to Theo's father: Voss. Theo intercepts the file and must choose between family and Odile. Beat: betrayal looms; Theo burns the file but can't unlearn the name.

chapters.title: Midterm Presentation
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Their project presentation on 'civic institutions' becomes a veiled indictment of the Tryouts; Mr. Okafor gives them an A and a warning. Beat: they've crossed from observers to participants.

chapters.title: The Trap
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The committee leaks a fake scandal to flush out the ghost; Odile walks into it and is suspended pending 'an integrity review.' Beat: lowest point; isolation, the cost of exposure.

chapters.title: Whose Side Are You On
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo confronts his father, who offers him the scholarship and Odile's silence in exchange for denouncing her publicly. Beat: duty versus love made explicit; Theo refuses.

chapters.title: Everything Is Fine
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Suspended and doxxed by rumor, Odile drafts a full confession post—every name, every document—then hesitates when she learns Theo could be expelled as her accomplice. Beat: sacrifice crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Assembly
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: at the pre-Tryouts assembly, Theo takes the stage and outs himself as co-author of the investigation before the committee can expel Odile alone. Odile follows, publishing the archive live. Beat: truth detonates in public.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unscripted
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fallout: the committee resigns, Dana's name is restored to the 1987 yearbook, and Odile's suspension is overturned—but Theo's father cuts him off completely. Beat: victory with real costs; found family gathers at the diner.

chapters.title: A New Rubric
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Students, Dana, and Mr. Okafor rebuild the Tryouts with open scoring and student seats on the committee. Theo and Odile finally kiss, off-script. Beat: hope institutionalized; love chosen freely.

chapters.title: Signed, Odile Voss
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Graduation: the final yearbook page carries both their names, and @yearbookghost signs off with one last post—a thank-you note to the town. Beat: resolution, identity claimed, future open.
